Brief: Tell me about Alan Turing and elaborate on the impact of his work. — about Homosexuality and indecency conviction

1. In December 1951, Turing met Arnold Murray, a 19-year-old unemployed man.
2. Turing was walking along Manchester's Oxford Road when he met Murray just outside the Regal Cinema and invited him to lunch.
3. The two agreed to meet again and in January 1952 began an intimate relationship.
4. On 23 January, Turing's house in Wilmslow was burgled.
5. Murray told Turing that he and the burglar were acquainted, and Turing reported the crime to the police.
6. During the investigation, he acknowledged a sexual relationship with Murray.
7. Initial committal proceedings for the trial were held on 27 February during which Turing's solicitor "reserved his defence", i.e., did not argue or provide evidence against the allegations.
8. The proceedings were held at the Sessions House in Knutsford.
9. Turing was later convinced by the advice of his brother and his own solicitor, and he entered a plea of guilty. The case, Regina v.
10. Turing and Murray, was brought to trial on 31 March 1952.
11. Turing's barrister pushed for him not to be incarcerated, and he was sentenced to 12 months' probation.
12. His probation would be conditional on his agreement to undergo organotherapy or 'chemical castration' in the Manchester Royal Infirmary, a process which induces hormonal physical changes with the aim of reducing libido.
